selected.title: The camera count is not the fire count
selected.texas_link: The Xcel program serves the Texas Panhandle, while Moore County is a named county in the SPS resiliency report. No camera position is assigned to Moore County.

movement.action: filed its first annual resiliency report

selected.why_today: The Docket admitted the report comparison on September 28th after September reporting renewed scrutiny of Panhandle wildfire mitigation. The May filing is identified as older evidence.
selected.consequence: Residents and fire crews need usable warning, while installation counts alone do not establish the number of camera detections.
selected.application_change: AI cameras are intended to recognize smoke and pass possible fires to a command center for response.
selected.counter_image: The annual report covers a partial year and counts installed cameras in place of the requested detection count. That absence does not establish zero detections.
selected.earned_take: An installed camera is one step toward warning. This report does not supply the outcome count required to evaluate its detections.

agency.next_step: Readers can inspect the public report and ask the commission or utility about the detection metric.
agency.who_can_act: Utility reporting personnel and the Public Utility Commission can address the requested metric.

action_proposals.visible_action: An illustrated smoke column rises into a camera view. Its image is carried to a review surface, then physical installation symbols are separated from an explicitly unreported detection total.
action_proposals.consequence: The intended camera workflow gives analysts a possible fire image, but installed equipment and documented detections remain distinct evidence categories.
action_proposals.limits: Original explanatory geometry only. No actual fire, camera site, proprietary software, human response or measured successful detection is reconstructed. Camera imagery is not a confirmed fire and an empty report field is not zero detections.
action_proposals.source_basis: SPS describes smoke detection, fire identification and command-center notification. Xcel supplies Panhandle geography and human verification. PUCT requires detection counts; SPS supplies installed cameras for a partial reporting year. Every illustrated relationship is bound to these fetched claims.
action_proposals.disclosure: Illustration. Schematic symbols and intended workflow

visual_stakes.affected_person: Panhandle residents and fire crews who need an actionable warning of a possible wildfire.
visual_stakes.physical_subject: A horizon-scanning camera, a smoke plume and the reported installation category.
visual_stakes.visible_change: The smoke rises into view, a captured image moves to review, then the installation marker separates from the missing detection total.
visual_stakes.consequence: Residents and fire crews need usable warning, while installation counts alone do not establish the number of camera detections.
visual_stakes.opening_question: Does installing a smoke camera establish how many fires it detected?
visual_stakes.answer: The report counts installed cameras but does not give the fire-detection total.
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Original source-grounded explanatory geometry fits the intended workflow. Available press imagery lacks established reuse rights and supplies no actual Texas response.
